newsitem.title: UK: HORSE RACING-SWAIN SWINGING IN THE RAIN.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-SWAIN SWINGING IN THE RAIN.

text.p: It was meant to be horse racing's version of the Three Tenors -- celebrated international virtuosi at one of the world's most famous venues.
But the principals -- Singspiel, Helissio and Pilsudski -- were outsung by a member of the chorus, albeit a very talented one, in the shape of the 16-1 outsider Swain.
On ground softened by an early afternoon downpour, Swain, ridden by John Reid, battled home a length clear of Pilsudski with Helissio third and Singspiel fourth.
Ascot's King George VI and Queen Elizabeth Diamond Stakes, billed as one of the great races of all time, was to have settled the champion of champions.

What emerged was another champion, reaping rich rewards for superb consistency which has seen him never out of the money in a career in which he has campaigned at the very highest level. Earnings now stand at more than $900,000.
The rain was the critical factor enabling Swain to reverse Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe form with Helissio and Pilsudski who had both beaten him convincingly in better ground at Longchamp last October.

Helissio, backed down to 11-10 favourite, tried to make all the running along with Kingfisher Mill but had little left when Swain took over with 300 metres to run. Losing jockey Cash Asmussen said: "Helissio has run an extremely courageous race and has been beaten by a champion today."

Swain, once trained in France, is now part of the Godolphin team of Sheikh Mohammed who had three other horses running for him in the eight-strong field -- fourth-placed Singspiel, Shantou (fifth) and Predappio (seventh).

Godolphin racing manager Simon Crisford disclosed that Swain had worked really well at home recently but added: "I am a little bit surprised (he won) because whenever he has run in this type of race he has been found wanting. He seemed to lack that bit extra but clearly we were wrong."
Sheikh Mohammed said: "I thought before the rain came that Singspiel was our best but because of the ground his chance went. But Swain loved the ground."
Reid, successful in 1978 on Ile de Bourbon, said: "They called it the race of the century and I can't believe I won it."
Like Swain, Eclipse Stakes and Breeders' Cup Turf winner Pilsudski will probably head for the 1997 Arc.
"It was a race for men," said Pilsudski's trainer Michael Stoute. "They were both very brave and they have run their hearts out."

Jockey Frankie Dettori blamed the ground for the disappointing showing of Singspiel, never out of the first two in his previous 14 outings. The ebullient Italian said: "He can't cope with it. He's too good a mover and had no more to give in the last furlong."
The Japan and Dubai World Cup winner could now be aimed at the Breeders' Cup.
